summary: FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026) crop 22,647.49 t, 23.69 t/ha: 16% below the 28.25 t/ha budget and 18% below 28.99 t/ha the year before (PA). Agro: fewer bunches per palm (10.86 vs 15.59) despite heavier bunches (15.30 vs 13.07 kg).

Harvesters rose from 135 (Apr) to 179 (Jul 2026), but harvesting intervals were 13–24 days in April and still delayed in July, leaving loose fruit and hanging dried fronds (PA, Aug 2026).
Manuring 100% of the 1,406.73 mt programme; leaf P is the main limiting nutrient, N marginal (Agro). No change to the 2026/27 programme.
Glyphosate overspray and a 3-month dry spell left about 20% of ground bare; mechanised infield collection pilot started July 2026; new Estate Manager from August 2026.

issues.title: Harvester ratio: 1:16 or 1:18 ha
issues.detail: PA 4.3 and 7.2: 179 harvesters in July 2026 = 1 harvester to 16 ha. PA concluding remark 13.4 says the same 179 harvesters give 1 to 18 ha. 2,886.45 ha / 179 = 16.1 ha, so 13.4 is wrong.

issues.detail: PA Table 11: Div 4 subtotal cost IDR 470,148 (RM106.63) per ha per round and grand total IDR 814,644 (RM184.76), while the block rows are IDR 88,410–152,698 and other divisions' subtotals are IDR 82,153–96,480. actions.item: Tighten spraying supervision and retrain sprayers to stop glyphosate overspray and bare ground
Raise sprayer productivity from 3.0 to 5.0 ha per man-day
Spray noxious broadleaf weeds with Ally 20DF and/or Triclopyr by mist blower; Stenochlaena and sedges with paraquat + Ally
Bring harvesting interval below 15 days with the extra harvesters and mechanised infield collection; deploy manuring workers to loose fruit
Monitor the mechanised infield collection pilot (productivity, method, vehicle running cost)
Remove hanging dried fronds once harvesting intervals are normal; harvesters to cut them with ripe bunches
Surface raised collection roads with laterite during the dry weather
Mechanise compost distribution with the estate's rubber-tracked vehicles
Keep vehicle and machinery maintenance on schedule (running costs over budget)
Strengthen boundary trenches and security patrols against FFB theft
Consolidate small sub-blocks into 40–60 ha management units for leaf sampling
Infill DI15-08A1 (126 SPH) and DG18-23A1 (125 SPH)
Avoid lumpy fertiliser application; spread evenly on the inner circle edge next to frond stacks
Apply compost on higher ground, in thin layers, possibly in alternate years, to limit Ganoderma and rhinoceros beetle risk
Cut over-ripe bunches (5–9%) and recover bunches fallen into drains
Switch to a second-generation rat bait so it lasts 7 days between replacements
Control Molineria latifolia in DK22-12A1 with 2,4-D amine + Garlon or glyphosate + Garlon
Encourage Nephrolepis ground cover in low-lying areas
Continue thinning runt palms (645 removed in FY2025/26)
Set up a 1–2 sub-block trial of Asian Agri virescent material at the next replanting
Glyphosate only on the 2.0 m circle and on lalang, Pennisetum, giant paspalum; spray harvester paths 1.2 m wide only where grass is dense
Raise worker pay through productivity: mechanisation and longer working hours
Raise, compact and cure the remaining collection roads for 3–6 months, then laterite them next FY
Keep the water table 50–75 cm below ground; hold water in field drains in the dry spell
Increase harvesters to at least 160 (1 to 18 ha) — 179 by July 2026
Re-establish the mechanised infield collection team — 2 MTG gangs started July 2026
Collect loose fruit promptly and deliver the same day to cut partially rotten loose fruit
Extend the recommended frond stacking method to larger areas
Use mist blowers with a one-sided nozzle cover or baffle for selective interrow spraying
Blanket spraying of tall grass only as a correction, followed by selective weeding
Monitor and promptly eradicate localised weed patches, especially seed-spreading species
In ex-rehab areas with yellow, small-canopy palms keep green fronds; remove only dry fronds
Close the gap between scheduled and actual fertiliser rounds; never apply on waterlogged ground
Catch up the delayed RP application flagged at 2-2025
Monitor and maintain drains so they run freely (high water table)
